name: Modern SEO - M1L5 The Low Competition Ranking Method
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 1 Foundation and Diagnosis](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-1-foundation-and-diagnosis) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
The three-step method in detail (4:41). Claimed to work for 70 to 80% of local businesses in markets under 500,000 people without intense competition ("plumbers, roofers, dentists"), but not for niches like personal injury lawyers in Manhattan. Module 2 shows each step over the shoulder.

# The three steps
1. **GBP audit.** Categories and services spot on. Google allows up to 10 categories and dozens of services; "every additional category and service is another opportunity for Google to show your business." Relevant and accurate only. The primary category matters most and should match what people search (HVAC example: "air conditioning repair"). "Changing primary categories is a big deal and can disrupt existing rankings": change only if clearly wrong or rankings are terrible.
2. **GBP landing page audit** (the page the GBP links to, usually the homepage). Highlights (the full audit checks "way more than five things"):
   - LocalBusiness schema
   - Phone matches the GBP
   - Address matches exactly
   - GBP map embedded
   - Primary category + city in the title tag and H1
3. **Super citations.** Verified profiles on platforms that require verification, such as Apple Maps and Bing Places. "The difference between regular citations and super citations is this verification." Free if done manually; the instructor uses LeadSnap (paid), which he says copies the GBP to 51 verification-required platforms and lets you skip or automate verification.

# Checklist
- Market check: under 500,000 people, not intense competition.
- All relevant categories (up to 10) and services listed; primary category matches searches and is left alone if ranking well.
- Landing page: schema, phone, exact address, GBP embed, title tag and H1 with primary category + city.
- Verified profiles on Apple Maps, Bing Places and others.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Plumbers are named as a best fit, which suits [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub). Kim can judge each client's market size to predict whether later phases will be needed.
- Review each client's [Google Business Profile](lib:brain-google-business-profile) categories and services against what the client really offers.
- **Alphalete phone match:** the site schema carries three different phone numbers and the official number awaits confirmation; the Alphalete lesson fix-steps file says to hold citation work until one number is decided. See [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and [Lesson Takeaways 2026-10-08](lib:brain-lesson-takeaways-2026-10-08).
- **Summit AZ phone match:** compare the HTML/schema number (480) 447-7008 to the GBP, not the GHL tracking number shown in the browser; do not touch the tracking snippet.
- For [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub) and all clients: check whether Apple Maps and Bing Places are claimed and verified (free route) before any paid tool. Findings go to Kim as a fix list.

# Caveats and open questions
- The landing page slide skips number 4 (1, 2, 3, 5, 6); only five items exist.
- Audio says "10 primary categories"; a GBP has one primary category, so the slide's "10 categories" is likely right. Check against Google's current rules.
- The LeadSnap skip-verification claim needs checking, and LeadSnap is paid (Kim's approval required).
